sources.sourceText:
Step 4.3: Choosing company directors & other key officers
Last updated on 29 January 2026.

Note: Every company must have at least one company director and one company secretary.
A secretary must be appointed within six months of successful registration. The position cannot be empty for more than six months. Otherwise, the director may face a fine of up to $1,000.

(Required) Company secretary
Company secretaries help the company to comply with its requirements.

Eligibility requirements
A company secretary must:
Be a real person (not a company).
Be a Singapore citizen, Singapore permanent resident, or someone who meets local residency rules.
Not be the same person as the sole director.

Roles and responsibilities
Company secretaries handle administrative work, including:
Maintaining their local company's information and registers.
Maintaining their foreign company's information.
Organising meetings and taking notes.
Reminding directors about annual filing deadlines.
Updating everyone on any new rules.

sources.sourceText:
An annual return is an online form you have to file with ACRA.

It contains key details about your company, such as:

Company name and registration number

Company type, business activities, and registered office address

Details of directors, the company secretary, and members

Share information and financial statements (if required)

This information helps stakeholders (like investors and partners) to make informed decisions.

Annual filing requirements

Company officers must file annual returns on time to avoid enforcement action.

Company requirements

Filing requirement

Details

Annual return filing with ACRA

All companies registered in Singapore must file an annual return with ACRA each year. This applies as long as your company is listed as “live” with us.

You must file an annual return even if your company is:

Inactive or dormant

Granted a tax waiver by the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS)

Filing your annual return keeps your company’s public information accurate. As a director, it is your legal duty to file on time.

Tax filing with IRAS

After filing your annual return, you must still file your taxes with IRAS. Check IRAS filing due dates and guides (opens in new tab).

Note: Dormant companies must also file tax returns unless IRAS has granted a waiver. Learn more about filing requirements for dormant companies (opens in new tab).

When to file your annual returns

Your deadline for filing the Annual Return is based on:

Your company's FYE

Your company type (listed or non-listed company)

Filing deadlines

Company type

Filing deadline

Listed companies

Within five months after FYE

Listed companies with:

A share capital

An overseas branch register

Within six months after FYE

Non-listed companies

Within seven months after FYE

Non-listed companies with:

A share capital

An overseas branch register

Within eight months after FYE

Note: You must file your annual returns on time to avoid penalties. You cannot change your FYE after the filing deadline has passed.

outcomes.question: For our company's current ECI filing, annual revenue is S$4.8 million and the accounts show a loss. We have not completed the tax adjustments. Is that enough to claim the filing waiver, or what still needs checking?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### IRAS — Corporate income tax

**Status:** Evidence verified

**ECI filing and waiver requirements** (party in scope: Company)
- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS generally requires ECI filing within three months after FYE. The general waiver requires both annual revenue of S$5 million or less for that financial year and nil ECI for the YA, with ECI measured before partial or start-up exemption. Revenue is the company’s main source of income; for an investment holding company it is investment income. A nil ECI or book loss alone does not qualify a company whose relevant revenue exceeds S$5 million; likewise, revenue below the threshold does not qualify when ECI is positive. IRAS gives separate entity categories that need not file and says companies self-assess the waiver. To assess a particular YA, confirm FYE, principal/investment revenue, pre-exemption ECI and any specifically excluded category. [IRAS | Estimated Chargeable Income (ECI) Filing](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/corporate-income-tax/estimated-chargeable-income-(eci)-filing)

**Source:** IRAS | Estimated Chargeable Income (ECI) Filing (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ECI filing and waiver requirements): ECI is an estimate of your company's taxable profits (after deducting tax-allowable expenses) for a Year of Assessment (YA).
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ECI filing and waiver requirements): Your company has to file ECI within 3 months from the end of your financial year unless: • Your company qualifies for the ECI filing waiver; or • Your company is specifically not required to file ECI.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports ECI filing and waiver requirements): Your company does not need to file ECI in any Year of Assessment (YA) when both criteria are met: • Annual revenue1 is $5 million or below for the financial year; and • ECI is nil for the YA. sources.sourceText:
ECI is an estimate of your company's taxable profits (after deducting tax-allowable expenses) for a Year of Assessment (YA).

Your company has to file ECI within 3 months from the end of your financial year unless: • Your company qualifies for the ECI filing waiver; or • Your company is specifically not required to file ECI.

Your company does not need to file ECI in any Year of Assessment (YA) when both criteria are met: • Annual revenue1 is $5 million or below for the financial year; and • ECI is nil for the YA. The ECI should be the amount before deducting the exempt amount under the partial tax exemption scheme or the tax exemption scheme for new start-up companies.

Revenue refers to a company's main source of income and excludes separate source income, such as interest, dividend and rental, which does not arise from its principal activity. In the case of an investment holding company, the revenue is its investment income (e.g. dividend income and interest income).

Your company is required to self-assess if it qualifies for the ECI filing waiver.

If your company falls within 1 of the following categories, it does not need to file ECI: • Foreign ship owners or charterers whose local shipping agent has submitted/ will submit the Shipping Return (PDF, 104KB) • Foreign universities • Designated unit trusts and approved CPF unit trusts# • Real estate investment trusts that have been granted the tax treatment under Section 43(2) of the Income Tax Act 1947 • Cases specifically granted the waiver to furnish ECI by IRAS

If your company's ECI is nil and its annual revenue is more than $5 million, you are still required to file the ECI.

All other parameters will remain unchanged.

- **IRAS rule explanation:** IRAS states that staff medical input tax is generally disallowed under regulation 26 of the GST (General) Regulations. Input tax claims are disallowed under Regulation 26 of the GST (General) Regulations.

However, subject to the conditions for input tax claim, these claims are allowed if: • the medical expenses (e.g. pre-employment and annual health screening expenses) are obligatory under the Work Injury Compensation Act (WICA) or under any collective agreement under the Industrial Relations Act (IRA); or • the medical treatment in respect of expenses incurred on or after 1 Oct 2021 is provided in connection with any health risk or requirement due to the work nature or environment and mandated by written law or advisory.

No, GST incurred on PCP will not be claimable. outcomes.question: Our employee must repay a conditional bonus after failing its service condition. CPF was paid eighteen months ago, but the employment agreement does not state a repayment date and we have not agreed one with the employee. Is a CPF refund necessarily out of time?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Compliance & Legal Authority

**Whole-question status:** Verified general guidance is available. Evidence verified for mapped issues; full request coverage unconfirmed.

**General statutory guidance:** Verified for all listed issues.
**Individual applicability:** General guidance does not by itself establish eligibility or compliance in an individual case.
**Material evidence gaps:** None identified within the listed guidance. Full request coverage still requires an independent assessment.

#### CPF Board — CPF contributions

**Status:** Evidence verified

**CPF employer refund timing and application requirements** (party in scope: Employer)
- **CPF rule explanation:** Refund requests for CPF contributions generally must be made immediately and no later than one year from payment; the “PAYMENTS RECEIVED ON” field identifies the payment date. For conditional wages, the one-year period instead runs from when the wages are due to be repaid to the employer, as stated in employment terms or a mutual agreement, and that date must be entered in the application. Before applying, the employer must return the employee share directly to the employee. CPF Board effects refunds only to the extent of funds available in the employee’s CPF account. Excess Additional Wage ceiling contributions should be claimed promptly; excess CPF Annual Limit contributions paid from 2023 are automatically refunded to the employer’s Direct Debit Account from February 2024. The general and entire-submission application deadline is one year from contribution payment, using the “PAYMENTS RECEIVED ON” record field. Conditional-wage refunds use the repayment due date, not the contribution payment date. The employer must first return the employee share where applicable; refunds depend on funds available in employee CPF accounts. Excess Additional Wage ceiling contributions are a prompt-application category. CPF Annual Limit excess contributions paid from 2023 are refunded automatically to the employer from February 2024; this is distinct from an application for an AW-ceiling refund. For case-specific application, consider: Refund category and CPF payment date. For conditional wages, the contractual or mutually agreed repayment due date. Whether the employee share was returned and funds remain available in CPF account(s). For AW or annual-limit excess, the relevant year and excess category. Do not infer a refund deadline when the payment date, conditional-wage repayment date or calendar anniversary is unclear. The source does not establish that a particular refund application will be accepted or the amount CPF Board will refund. [CPFB | Applying for refund of CPF contributions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/compliance-and-rectifications/applying-for-refund-of-cpf-contributions)

**Source:** CPFB | Applying for refund of CPF contributions (live external)
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Any request for refund of CPF contributions paid must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date of payment of the CPF contributions. You can refer to the “PAYMENTS RECEIVED ON” field in your record of payment to determine the date of payment.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Any request for refund of CPF contributions paid on conditional wages must be made immediately and no later than one year from the date wages are supposed to be repaid to the employer. This will be the date stated in the terms of employment or based on mutual agreement
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): You’re responsible to refund the employee’s share of CPF contributions (where applicable) directly to your employee before submitting the application.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Refund is subject to availability of funds
We’ll effect the refund based on the available funds in the employee’s CPF account
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Refund of payments made in excess of Additional Wage ceiling
Once you have discovered that you paid CPF contributions in excess of the AW ceiling for any of your employees, you should apply for a refund of the CPF contributions made promptly.
- **Verified official source excerpt** (supports CPF employer refund timing and application requirements): Refund of contributions paid in excess of CPF Annual Limit
From February 2024, any CPF contributions paid in excess of the CPF Annual Limit will be refunded automatically to the employer's Direct Debit Account maintained with CPF Board. This applies to excess contributions paid from year 2023
- Official source: [CPFB | Applying for refund of CPF contributions](https://www.cpf.gov.sg/employer/compliance-and-rectifications/applying-for-refund-of-cpf-contributions)

outcomes.question: An employee covered by the Employment Act has completed four months of service, supplied the required medical certificate and informed us within twenty-four hours. Is the statutory entitlement already fourteen outpatient sick-leave days plus sixty hospitalisation days?
outcomes.answer:
### Statutory Directive: Annual Leave and Paid Sick / Hospitalisation Leave Statutory Entitlements

**Governing Authority**: **MOM** | **Legislation**: **Employment Act 1968 (Section 88A & Section 89)**

---

#### 1. Statutory Principle
Employees covered by the Employment Act 1968 who have served an employer for at least 3 months are entitled to paid sick leave. Employees who have served for at least 12 months are entitled to statutory paid annual leave.

---

#### 2. Key Rules, Thresholds & Compliance Mandates
* Paid Annual Leave (Section 88A): Minimum 7 days after 1 year of service, increasing by 1 additional day per completed year of service, up to a statutory maximum of 14 days for 8 or more years of service.
* Paid Outpatient Sick Leave (Section 89): Up to 14 days per calendar year if certified by an approved medical practitioner. Graduated during first 6 months of employment (5 days at 3 months, 8 days at 4 months, 11 days at 5 months, 14 days at 6+ months).
* Paid Hospitalisation Leave (Section 89): Up to 60 days per calendar year (which includes the 14 days of outpatient sick leave).
* Public Holidays (Section 88): 11 statutory gazetted public holidays per year. If required to work on a public holiday, an employee is entitled to an extra day of basic salary or a day off in lieu.

---

#### 3. Official Statutory Source & Verification
* Verified against Employment Act 1968 Section 88A & Section 89 using the registered official source record.

sources.sourceText:
If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.

If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.

If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations .

sources.sourceText:
If your company wishes to conduct fund management activities regulated under the Securities and Futures Act 2001 (SFA) , it must apply to be a licensed fund management company (LFMC) that holds a capital markets services (CMS) licence.

If your company solely manages venture capital funds, it may apply to be an LFMC that operates under the simplified venture capital fund manager (VCFM) regime.

Individuals performing key functions in a fund management company, such as portfolio construction and allocation, research and advisory, business development and marketing or client servicing are required to be representatives.

You can find out more about fund management activity and the differences between an LFMC and VCFM here.

When we assess your company to be an LFMC or VCFM, MAS considers factors such as:

• Credibility and substantiveness of the business model and plan, and the associated risks;

• Effectiveness of risk management and compliance controls;

• Fund management track record and expertise of an LFMC applicant's management, parent company and major shareholders;

• Fitness and propriety of the applicant, its shareholders and directors; and

• Ability to meet the relevant minimum financial requirements prescribed under the SFA.

In addition, your company needs to operate from a dedicated and secure office space that is accessible only by your company’s directors and staff.

For more information on the admission criteria and applicable requirements, please refer to the Guidelines on Licensing and Conduct of Business for Fund Management Companies.

VCFMs are subject to a simplified set of admission criteria – please refer to Appendix 4 of the aforementioned guidelines.

If your company is able to operate under an existing class exemption, it does not require a licence. Examples of companies that may be eligible for exemption include those that:

• Manage assets for related corporations or related family members;

• Manage a pool of immovable assets for accredited and institutional investors; or

• Manage a pool of non-capital markets products for accredited and institutional investors.

You can find more information on exemptions under section 99 of the SFA and paragraph 5 of the Second Schedule to the Securities and Futures (Licensing and Conduct of Business) Regulations .
